claims.claim: Real planets show internally consistent transit geometry: the stellar density implied by the transit (period, duration, impact parameter, radius ratio) matches the catalog star's density from logg and radius. Eclipsing binaries and blends tend to break this consistency. They also tend to have grazing geometry (b + k > 1), a depth that disagrees with k^2, or an implied radius that is not planetary.

Real planets differ from eclipsing binaries and blends in ways the incumbent's transit-shape and host-star features only partly capture. Centroid shifts, odd-even depth mismatch, single/multiple-event statistics and candidate multiplicity (koi_count) carry that information. Native-NaN gradient boosting plus a random forest handles the many missing values better than median imputation alone.
